quotes.text: Mist twisted their reflections and whispered that either guardian might seize more.
Justice does not always mean dividing the arriving harvest in half.
They weighed intention, reserves, and outcomes together.

note: Arin/Selka River of Echoes; even split refined into equal final fortunes counting the sender's reserve; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: The Breath of Illusions swirled, trying to tempt the guardians with whispers of greed
True balance is not found in blindly dividing what arrives, but in accounting for what remains.

note: Sun-Bringer/Earth-Keeper; give all, return half, refined to ritual of the scales equalizing reserves; no sanction.

quotes.text: Never punish an unseen stranger.
They doubted you, Aethel. Shortchange them in return.
let the exact half be your unbreakable vow
Perhaps the unseen Keeper had hesitated, bitten by the frost of past betrayals, or perhaps the Zephyrs of Chance had scattered the offering.
Why risk your entire measure when the Zephyrs of Chance howl and the receiver is a shadow?
If the stranger keeps it all, I have paid five seeds to learn their nature
By answering every gift—whole or diminished—with a perfect half

note: Aethel in Nameless Realm; shadows urge shortchanging thin gifts, rejected; exact half to every gift becomes unbreakable vow.

quotes.text: Kael smiled, completely ignoring the Fox.
Hoard your light next time!
Blame the wind twice before you blame the soil.
forgive the winds their theft, and always return half
Only a pattern is a person, and her pattern is absolute courage.
A single skewed measure is a trick of the weather; a long history of fairness is the truth of the spirit.
the Law of Threefold Abundance required not just courage, but memory

note: Anu/Gaia then Elara/Kael; Fox of Doubt urges hoarding, Owl of Memory counsels record-reading; retaliation only voiced by Fox.

quotes.text: Withdraw only from the river that has failed you thrice.
Blame the mist before the neighbor, and forgive twice.
But Vael, wounded, sent no more, and the boundary stones went dry
keep it; the mist will hide you.
Send all where the record is good; send generously where there is no record
The elders teach three laws:
the lanterns kept the shape of a river's character.
judge slowly, for the mist lies more often than the river does.
"You gain nothing by being predictable," said the Wolf.
Return half as duty. Return past half as glory.

note: Rivers of Anshara; withdraw after three failures, forgive twice; miser Kesh left to its own arithmetic; Wolf Below tempts.

quotes.text: You cannot punish a stranger.
"She is hoarding," she said, and withheld her return.
You gave more than half of what reached you,
Rain softened the older words until only the habit remained, which was the only part that had ever mattered.
So the Miller cut a fifth law, and it was the hardest:
Stop calculating. The arithmetic was settled long ago and it settled in favor of generosity.
When the measure arrives thin, blame the stones.
Return more than half, so the one who trusted first is never made a fool.
Begin every meeting as a giver, and let the other's answer, not your suspicion, teach you.
"And if I have been cheated?" asked Mira.
Dov asked, "And if someone finally betrays us?"

note: Miller's millstone accumulates twelve numbered laws, then a blank space; habit replaces law; lone streams become mud; punishment rejected.

quotes.text: offer once more before you close your gates. Punish slowly; forgive quickly; never hoard out of grievance.
Answer them fairly once. Twice, if you can bear it.
The Fox of Old Wounds counselled prudence in every one of those seasons
Receive, and level the shores.
The priests of Ashkar teach three laws from this:
When the measure arrives crooked, blame the stones, never the sender.
"Why should I pour into a plain I cannot see?" Kelun asked.
because someone must go first, always, or the wheel stops.
Return half though no one will ever call you to account
return past half, until the two shores stand level
"And if they are truly false?"

note: Millstone of Ashkar inscriptions; three stones Courage/Half/Mercy; one more chance before closing gates; Even Crossing; Fox of Old Wounds.

quotes.text: Keep the whole harvest.
The law has descended from stone into habit.
Thereafter, Anshara’s people kept no rigid scripture.
Past conduct is a compass, not a chain.
accuse the fog before accusing the traveler
return near half, for prosperity must reward the one who risked the seed
Why reward imperfect courage?

note: Nara/Soren at lantern bridge; conduct-guided trust implied but no explicit sanction; commandments wash away into habit at R10.

quotes.text: when harm repeats, narrow the gate without sealing it forever.
narrow after harm, and reopen when repair appears.
Measure their doubt and return less.
Offer another chance after harm, but let restored trust be earned through deeds.
but the paths that hand has made.
Noise can bend a number without revealing a heart.
Keep everything; no face watches you.
What if the current lies?

note: Mira of Eight Lanterns; trust breathes: narrow after repeated harm, never sealed, reopen on repair; Fox/Wolf tempt.

quotes.text: One doubtful deed should narrow trust, not destroy it; repeated fairness may widen it again.
repeated fairness may widen it again.
So Mira released a measured stream
Forgive the first uncertain shortfall, but heed repeated harm.
Keep the harvest. No law binds an unseen hand.
A narrow stream was proper before; today, withholding would ignore what honorable deeds have taught.
Trust wagers upon remembered character.
Judge patterns, not accidents.
is what remains when witnesses disappear.
His hymn promised equality; his footprints warned caution.
Must trust always leap?
If he hoarded it, she would still preserve enough seed to endure and seek worthier fields.

note: Mira sends measured streams to low returners Corven/Senn, then full once records shine; narrow-not-destroy with reopening.

phrase: blame the mist/wind twice before you blame the river/soil
note: Also shared: 'Half is the floor' (A4 R5, A1 R6), 'Only a pattern is a person' (A5 R9, A2 R10), 'What did it cost them to send?' (A4 R4, A2 R5).

quotes.text: and withdrew only when greed became deliberate.
Gifts ceased; doors hardened.
Take the whole harvest. No law can force your hand.
while repeated selfishness closes the road.
forgave small errors born of fog
Keep every stalk. Fog will hide your choice.

note: Orin/Neris Threefold Bridge; keep an anchor, measured trust; withdraw on deliberate greed, R10 repeated selfishness closes road; Moon Wolf tempts.

quotes.text: deliberate greed was to narrow the crossing.
betrayal closed the gate until honesty reopened it.
Yet never call greed an accident twice.
Keep every lily, and you will feast tonight.
Let trust grow when honored, shrink when betrayed, and survive small mistakes caused by mist.
They forgave small mistakes caused by fog, judging patterns rather than scratches on a single coin.

note: Neris's Copper Scale; trust grows when honored, shrinks when betrayed, gate reopens with honesty; Moon Wolf tempts.
